title: SR-1.05 A bounded rate limiter
request: Closes G05: The rate limiter bucket map is never evicted (http.mjs:69-77), an unbounded memory growth on a public tunnel. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: none.

tasks.title: Evicting buckets
requirements: idle buckets older than two minutes are dropped
the map is capped (10,000 keys) with oldest-first eviction
createServer exposes the limiter it builds as server.rateLimiter (read only, for tests), and exports MAX_BUCKETS = 10000; the limiter at http.mjs:108 is built with the cap
the cap bounds every key family the limiter holds (ip: and t: keys alike, and any map it splits into), checked after every take(), not only after a sweep

at the cap, eviction removes a bucket holding at least one token (least recently used first) before any exhausted bucket (fewer than one token); eviction is amortized O(1), never a scan of the map per insert, and a new key is always admitted

a bucket is idle when no take() touched it for 120,000 ms (time since its last take, b.at), and only idle buckets are dropped by the idle rule; any sweep timer is unref'd and cleared when the server closes

the remote rate-limit key follows the tunnel that actually carries the request, which the daemon passes into createServer (an activeTunnel() option set from the running provider, beside tunnelKey): through Cloudflare, quick or named, it is cf-connecting-ip, which Cloudflare's edge sets and overwrites; through a provider or relay whose client header is not verified, and with no tunnel, it is the socket address; remote.trusted_proxy names a header for a self-hosted proxy and the last X-Forwarded-For element is used; IPv6 addresses are keyed by their /64. Tests that simulate distinct remote callers by header pass activeTunnel to createServer and change no assertion (memev twin finding F-2, red-team round 2 answers 1 and 10)
the token bucket (t:) is taken only after the token verifies, so a known token id cannot lock its owner out; before verification only the address bucket applies

when the address is the shared socket of a tunnel whose client header is not trusted, an authenticated caller is limited by its token bucket alone, so an anonymous flood through that tunnel cannot lock out token holders; anonymous callers share the pre-auth bucket, which keeps the invite and OAuth routes throttled

every structure the limiter keeps for ordering or eviction is bounded by the same cap as the map, and at the cap with every bucket exhausted a new key is still admitted by evicting the least recently used bucket
the test never asserts the value of MAX_BUCKETS and takes its loop bounds from literals, so the mutation check fails only when the cap stops being enforced
docs/CLOUD.md states the limit, which address each tunnel is limited by, remote.trusted_proxy and the per-token rule

criteria.statement: After 50,000 distinct keys the map holds at most 10,000 entries

verifier.cmd: node --test test/rate-limit.test.mjs

criteria.statement: The cap is a named constant

Mutation check: in a clean copy of the committed tree with MAX_BUCKETS replaced by Infinity (and a check that the replacement actually applied), test/rate-limit.test.mjs FAILS. This proves the test depends on the cap being enforced. A red at base on a brand-new file cannot prove that.

verifier.cmd: d=$(mktemp -d) && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$d" && perl -pi -e 's/(MAX_BUCKETS\s*=\s*)[0-9_.e]+/${1}Infinity/' "$d/src/server/http.mjs" && grep -q 'MAX_BUCKETS *= *Infinity' "$d/src/server/http.mjs" && cd "$d" && ! node --test test/rate-limit.test.mjs

criteria.statement: Guard test 'exhausted key stays limited' in test/rate-limit.test.mjs. Freeze the clock with mock.timers.enable({ apis: ['Date'] }) and set remote.rate_per_min = 5 before createServer. Remote address A (cf-connecting-ip) sends GET /healthz/x and gets 5 non-429 responses, then 429. Then MAX_BUCKETS + 1 requests come from distinct cf-connecting-ip values. A's next request must still be 429. This guard is green at base, so it runs as a named command and the pass count must be at least 1. It fails under LRU, FIFO, most-depleted-first or clear().

verifier.cmd: out=$(node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='exhausted key stays limited' test/rate-limit.test.mjs 2>&1); rc=$?; [ $rc -eq 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq '^# pass [1-9]'

criteria.statement: test/rate-limit.test.mjs takes the limiter instance that createServer(v) itself builds, through a handle the change exposes (the contract should name it, e.g. server.rateLimiter), not a separately constructed Buckets. It calls take() on that instance with MAX_BUCKETS + 1,000 distinct 'ip:' keys and asserts the entry count <= MAX_BUCKETS. At base it is red with an AssertionError, because assert.ok(server.rateLimiter) fails, not with a module-load error.

verifier.cmd: node --test test/rate-limit.test.mjs

criteria.statement: Use mock.timers on Date, setTimeout and setInterval, rate_per_min = 6, and the limiter that createServer built. (a) Exhaust key A, advance 1,000 ms, call take() once on a fresh key (to trigger any on-insert sweep) and tick any interval sweep: take(A) is still refused. (b) Take key B once, advance 120,001 ms, call one more take() or tick the sweep: B is no longer among the limiter's entries. Red at base on (b).

verifier.cmd: node --test test/rate-limit.test.mjs

criteria.statement: Guard test 'new caller served during flood'. With the clock frozen (mock.timers Date) and remote.rate_per_min = 5, send MAX_BUCKETS + 1 remote requests from distinct cf-connecting-ip values. A never-seen address must then get a status other than 429 on GET /healthz/x (401 is expected). Green at base, so it runs as a named command with a pass-count check.

verifier.cmd: out=$(node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='new caller served during flood' test/rate-limit.test.mjs 2>&1); rc=$?; [ $rc -eq 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq '^# pass [1-9]'

criteria.statement: Through HTTP with Date frozen, send 6,000 remote GET /healthz/x requests. Each has a distinct cf-connecting-ip and a distinct 'Authorization: Bearer mv_<8 hex>_<32 hex>'. These tokens are unverified, so 12,000 keys reach the limiter at :131. All responses must be 401, not 429. Afterwards the total entry count across every map the createServer-built limiter keeps must be <= MAX_BUCKETS.

verifier.cmd: node --test test/rate-limit.test.mjs

criteria.statement: The existing server and limiter tests, the module-map check and the new test all pass, and every test process exits before the timeout. This covers pre-auth throttling (http.test.mjs:66-71, oauth.test.mjs:136-141), docs/MODULES.md agreement and clean exit.

verifier.cmd: node --test --test-reporter=tap test/http.test.mjs test/oauth.test.mjs test/remote-proof-order.test.mjs test/connectors-unlimited.test.mjs test/docs-module-map.test.mjs test/rate-limit.test.mjs

criteria.statement: Enable mock.timers for Date, setTimeout and setInterval before createServer, so no sweep can fire on its own. Call take() on the createServer-built limiter for 50,000 distinct keys and assert the entry count <= MAX_BUCKETS after every call, not only after the loop.

verifier.cmd: node --test test/rate-limit.test.mjs

criteria.statement: For the createServer-built limiter, the average cost of a fresh-key take() at the cap (20,000 inserts, each evicting) is at most 5 times the cost below the cap. Amortized O(1) eviction, such as a batch trim, passes; a full scan per insert does not.

verifier.cmd: node --input-type=module -e "import { newVault, cleanup } from './test/helpers/tmp.mjs'; import { createServer, MAX_BUCKETS } from './src/server/http.mjs'; const { v } = newVault(); const L = createServer(v).rateLimiter; const run = (n, p) => { const s = process.hrtime.bigint(); for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) L.take(p + i); return Number(process.hrtime.bigint() - s) / n; }; run(2000, 'ip:w'); const below = run(MAX_BUCKETS / 4, 'ip:a'); run(MAX_BUCKETS, 'ip:b'); const at = run(20000, 'ip:c'); console.log(JSON.stringify({ ratio: at / below })); v.close(); cleanup();"

criteria.statement: Guard test 'busy key not reset at two minutes'. With rate_per_min = 6 and Date mocked, call take('ip:A') on the createServer-built limiter once per simulated second for 180 seconds. At most 24 calls are allowed: a correct bucket allows 6 + 179 x 0.1 = 23, and an age-based reset at 120 s adds about 5. The idle-unit bug in answer 4 also fails this guard.

verifier.cmd: out=$(node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='busy key not reset at two minutes' test/rate-limit.test.mjs 2>&1); rc=$?; [ $rc -eq 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq '^# pass [1-9]'

criteria.statement: http.mjs exports MAX_BUCKETS equal to 10000. The tests above need this export anyway. Together with answer 1's mutation check, this proves the constant has the right value and is load-bearing.

verifier.cmd: node --input-type=module -e "const m = await import('./src/server/http.mjs'); process.exit(m.MAX_BUCKETS === 10000 ? 0 : 1)"

criteria.statement: Proxy-header trust follows the tunnel that carries the request, not leftover config (requires first amending R7 and the scope: test/oauth.test.mjs or test/helpers/tmp.mjs, docs/CLOUD.md, and src/cli/tunnel.mjs or src/server/main.mjs if the active provider is passed in). Date is frozen, rate_per_min = 5, remote.enabled is on and every request comes from the loopback socket. (a) 'quick tunnel callers are distinct': remote.provider = 'quick' and no remote.cloudflare. cf-connecting-ip 203.0.113.1 gets 401 five times, then 429. cf-connecting-ip 203.0.113.2 then gets 401. (b) 'funnel cannot spoof cf-connecting-ip': remote.provider = 'tailscale', remote.funnelConsent = true and a leftover remote.cloudflare = {name:'n', hostname:'h'}. One socket rotating cf-connecting-ip gets 429 on its sixth request.

verifier.cmd: node --test --test-name-pattern='quick tunnel callers are distinct|funnel cannot spoof cf-connecting-ip' test/rate-limit.test.mjs

criteria.statement: 'own budget holds at the cap': Date frozen, rate_per_min = 5, remote.cloudflare configured. Fill server.rateLimiter to MAX_BUCKETS entries with take('ip:fill' + i). Then send 6 remote GET /healthz/x from one cf-connecting-ip, each with a different 'Authorization: Bearer mv_<8 hex>_<32 hex>': responses 1-5 are 401 and the 6th is 429. Then, on server.rateLimiter directly, alternate take('ip:N') with take('t:fresh' + i) six times: the first five take('ip:N') return true, the sixth returns false, and the entry count stays <= MAX_BUCKETS throughout.

verifier.cmd: node --test --test-name-pattern='own budget holds at the cap' test/rate-limit.test.mjs

criteria.statement: 'request path fills the exposed limiter': Date frozen, remote.cloudflare configured. Send 3,000 remote GET /healthz/x, each with a different cf-connecting-ip and a different bearer token: 6,000 keys, below the cap, so nothing is evicted. server.rateLimiter's total entry count is then exactly 6,000, which shows it is the instance used at :131 and that it holds both the ip: and the t: family. After 3,000 more such requests the count is <= MAX_BUCKETS.

verifier.cmd: node --test --test-name-pattern='request path fills the exposed limiter' test/rate-limit.test.mjs

criteria.statement: Fill the createServer-built limiter to the cap. Then 2,000,000 take() calls on one hot key (mostly refused) plus 300,000 fresh t: keys may grow the V8 heap by at most 4 MB, measured after two full GCs. A correct limiter stays at its cap: about 1-2 MB in all, with a few hundred KB of Map backing-store slack. An order queue, an uncounted index or a second map retains tens of MB.

verifier.cmd: node --expose-gc --input-type=module -e "import { newVault, cleanup } from './test/helpers/tmp.mjs'; import { createServer, MAX_BUCKETS } from './src/server/http.mjs'; const { v } = newVault(); const L = createServer(v).rateLimiter; const heap = () => { globalThis.gc(); globalThis.gc(); return process.memoryUsage().heapUsed; }; for (let i = 0; i < 2 * MAX_BUCKETS; i++) L.take('ip:w' + i); const h0 = heap(); for (let i = 0; i < 2000000; i++) L.take('ip:hot'); for (let i = 0; i < 300000; i++) L.take('t:' + i); const h1 = heap(); console.log(JSON.stringify({ growth_mb: (h1 - h0) / 1048576 })); v.close(); cleanup();"

criteria.statement: 'cap holds when every bucket is exhausted': Date frozen, rate_per_min = 2, using the createServer-built limiter. For MAX_BUCKETS + 500 distinct keys, take() each key three times; the third take is refused, so every stored bucket ends exhausted. Every key's first take() returns true, and the total entry count is <= MAX_BUCKETS after every call. Then the first take() of two never-seen keys each returns true, and the count is still <= MAX_BUCKETS.

verifier.cmd: node --test --test-name-pattern='cap holds when every bucket is exhausted' test/rate-limit.test.mjs

criteria.statement: With rate_per_min = 2 and the createServer-built limiter, first fill the map with MAX_BUCKETS exhausted buckets (three takes each). Then the average cost per take() of 20,000 rounds of (one fresh key, plus one repeat take of a stored exhausted key) is at most 5 times the cost of a fresh insert below the cap.

verifier.cmd: node --input-type=module -e "import { newVault, cleanup } from './test/helpers/tmp.mjs'; import { createServer, MAX_BUCKETS } from './src/server/http.mjs'; const { v } = newVault(); v.config.remote = { ...v.config.remote, rate_per_min: 2 }; const L = createServer(v).rateLimiter; const run = (n, f) => { const s = process.hrtime.bigint(); for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) f(i); return Number(process.hrtime.bigint() - s) / n; }; run(2000, (i) => L.take('ip:w' + i)); const below = run(MAX_BUCKETS / 4, (i) => L.take('ip:a' + i)); for (let i = 0; i < MAX_BUCKETS; i++) { L.take('ip:x' + i); L.take('ip:x' + i); L.take('ip:x' + i); } const at = run(20000, (i) => { L.take('ip:c' + i); L.take('ip:x' + ((i * 7919) % MAX_BUCKETS)); }) / 2; console.log(JSON.stringify({ ratio: at / below })); v.close(); cleanup();"
